claims.text: In-situ SEM tensile testing combined with DIC can effectively uncover deformation mechanisms in FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
Localized strain phenomena in FeNiCrMn can be linked to microstructural heterogeneities using in-situ SEM and DIC.
The investigated FeNiCrMn alloy may contain defined grain boundaries and multiphase regions in its as-fabricated or thermally treated state.
A controlled uniaxial tensile load can be applied while high-resolution SEM images and DIC strain fields are acquired simultaneously.
Ambient or moderately controlled temperature minimizes external thermal effects during testing.
A sufficiently slow loading rate enables real-time capture of deformation.
Grain size mediates strain localization and overall plastic deformation in FeNiCrMn.
Grain-boundary character mediates strain localization and overall plastic deformation in FeNiCrMn.
Phase distribution mediates strain localization and overall plastic deformation in FeNiCrMn.
Under tensile loading, localized deformation initiates at specific microstructural sites.
Combining mechanical loading with localized strain mapping can elucidate correlations between microstructure and mechanical response.
In-situ SEM tensile testing with DIC will reveal heterogeneous deformation patterns in FeNiCrMn.
The revealed deformation patterns will correlate with microstructural features.
The method will provide quantitative data on local strain evolution and overall tensile properties.
Conventional bulk ex-situ tensile tests provide overall stress-strain behavior without spatially resolved information about deformation mechanisms.
The method's resolution is limited by SEM imaging and DIC capabilities.
Extremely fast deformation events may be missed by the method.
Nanoscale deformation events may be missed by the method.
Sample-preparation artifacts may influence the observed results.
Local strain fields should predict overall mechanical properties measured in bulk tests if the proposed linkage is valid.
